description:
Problem: the reviewer's verdict reaches the oracle as free text in OMP's final assistant message, so the oracle carries its own contract to make that text usable: the RESPONSE TEMPLATE section of standard.md, gate.md and deep.md; the response_template slot built and revalidated by render.response_template; RESPONSE_PLACEHOLDERS and the unpopulated-placeholder rejection in verdict.py; final-message extraction (extract_omp_text, omp_stream_without_answer); and fence stripping and duplicate-key rejection in parse_output. A reply that drifts from the skeleton is recorded absent (invalid), retried and escalated, and the skeleton can drift from the validator itself, as the concedes slot did, failing every reviewer the same way. OMP already validates structured output inside the session: its yield tool checks the payload against a schema and retries, and the SDK's createAgentSession takes outputSchema, outputSchemaMode "strict" and requireYieldTool. The command line the oracle runs (omp --print --mode json) has no equivalent flag: checked in 18.12.6 on 2026-10-23 and in 18.13.2 and 18.14.0 on 2026-10-30.

Not the fix: OMP's /review command (evaluated 2026-10-27). Under the oracle's flags it does not expand (--no-extensions keeps the prompt literal); it needs the task tool and a bundled reviewer agent that has bash; that reviewer's output schema is not enforced by default (it returned prose with no yield call); subagent tool calls never reach the parent event stream the evidence check reads; and an orchestrator model rewrites the brief before the reviewer sees it. A subagent route (an orchestrator holding only task that spawns a custom structured agent) keeps the last two defects and is rejected for the same reasons.

Outcome: one reviewer session whose verdict is a yield payload validated in strict mode, with schema 2 as the single source for both the prompt's output contract and validation. Delete the RESPONSE TEMPLATE sections, the response_template slot and its validation, the placeholder machinery, and whatever final-text JSON extraction, fence and duplicate-key handling the schema makes unreachable. Keep unchanged: computed decisions (code decides and the stricter outcome wins), read evidence from the same event stream (the yield call sits beside the reads), prior-defect and dispute rules a schema cannot express, absence classification, rounds, redaction and posting. A payload that still fails the schema after OMP's retries is absent (invalid), never a pass.

Decision gates:
1. Path. (a) OMP adds strict output-schema support to print and json mode and the policy pins a build that has it, or (b) the review driver runs the reviewer session through the pinned, integrity-checked SDK package. Filing the upstream request is an external action: the owner files it or names it in the current request. Record the choice, and the upstream link or SDK pin, in context. For (b), confirm before coding that the SDK event stream exposes tool calls and results with the fields evidence.py reads.
2. Schema parity. Express schema 2 in OMP's schema dialect (seven top-level keys, enums, exact prior-entry keys, end_line integer or null, boolean concedes) and list every rule the dialect cannot express; those stay in verdict.py.
3. Measurement. Replay the 2026-10-23 bench cases (#3286, #3248, #3337, #3339 and the planted PAGE_SIZE = 0 defect) per reviewer role through the review harness, comparing valid-verdict rate, planted-defect catch, turns and tokens with develop. Stop and ask the owner if catch drops. The runs spend gateway quota, so the owner approves the run budget first.

Prior art: the oracle used harness-native structured output before (Codex structured outputs, and Claude's structured_output, which verdict.parse_output still unwraps) and dropped it when it moved to OMP only (_project/decisions/oracle-review-protocol-2026-10-08.md).
